title: Big Witt vectors, Λ-rings and q-de Rham–Witt complexes
summary: Big Witt vectors on truncation sets, Λ-rings with Adams operations, and Wagner's m-truncated big q-Witt vectors and q-de Rham–Witt complexes, absolute and relative to a perfectly covered Λ-ring. The roadmap proves the structural theorems (augmented Koszul exactness, injectivity of Verschiebungen and of W_m into q-W_m, joint injectivity of ghost maps, étale base change, rational ghost isomorphisms, arithmetic fracture squares). Its main theorem identifies the (q−1)-completed q-de Rham–Witt complex of a smooth framed algebra with the cohomology of its framed q-Hodge complex modulo q^m−1. It also builds the animated Nygaard filtrations and proves Wagner's no-go theorem for a functorial q-Hodge complex. These are the root-of-unity specialisations of Habiro rings and Habiro cohomology.
readme:
# Big Witt vectors, Λ-rings and q-de Rham–Witt complexes

## Purpose

This roadmap builds the algebra behind the specialisations of Habiro cohomology at roots of unity. It develops
big Witt vectors on truncation sets, Λ-rings with their Adams operations, and Ferdinand Wagner's
$m$-truncated big $q$-Witt vectors and $q$-de Rham–Witt complexes, absolute and relative to a Λ-ring
(Wagner, *q-Witt vectors and q-Hodge complexes*, arXiv:2410.23078v5). The main theorem is Wagner's
Theorem 4.27. Let $A$ be a perfectly covered Λ-ring, $R$ a smooth $A$-algebra with an étale framing $\square$ and
$m \ge 1$. Then the $q$-FV-system map
$$\big(q\text{-}W_m\Omega^*_{R/A}\big)^\wedge_{(q-1)} \longrightarrow H^*\big(q\text{-}\mathrm{Hdg}^*_{R/A,\square}/(q^m-1)\big)$$
is an isomorphism for every $m$, compatibly with Frobenii and Verschiebungen. The roadmap also proves the
no-go theorem (Wagner Theorem 5.1): these isomorphisms cannot be realised by a functor on smooth $A$-algebras
unless $A$ is a $\mathbb Q$-algebra.

Two consumers need these objects. The relative Habiro ring of `HabiroRings` satisfies
$\mathcal H_{R/A,m}/(q^m-1) \cong q\text{-}W_m(R/A)$ for étale $R$ (Wagner, *q-Hodge complexes over the Habiro ring*,
arXiv:2510.04782v2, Theorem 2.9). The Habiro–Hodge complex of `HabiroCohomologyFoundations` has, modulo
$q^m-1$, a filtration whose graded pieces are the shifted animated $q$-de Rham–Witt forms (same paper,
Theorem 3.11(b)).

## Scope

In scope:

- truncation sets and big Witt vectors $W_S$ with ghost map, Frobenius, Verschiebung, restriction and
  Teichmüller maps, the power-series description, the $p$-typical decomposition, the comonad structure and
  étale base change (Hesselholt, *The big de Rham–Witt complex*, §1);
- Λ-rings in Borger's sense, Adams operations, Wilkerson's criterion, truncated Λ$_m$-structures, and perfect
  and perfectly covered Λ-rings;
- Wagner's §§2–5 in full: $q$-FV-systems, absolute and relative $q$-Witt vectors, their ghost and
  comparison maps, étale morphisms, $q$-V- and $q$-FV-systems of differential-graded algebras,
  $q$-de Rham–Witt complexes with their Frobenii, étale base change and rational ghost isomorphisms;
- the framed $q$-de Rham and $q$-Hodge complexes of a framed smooth algebra, Theorem 4.27 with its
  arithmetic fracture squares, and the no-go Theorem 5.1;
- the animated $q$-de Rham–Witt complexes with their Nygaard and Hodge$_m$ filtrations, from the $q$-Hodge
  paper: 3.21, Lemmas 3.23, 3.24, 3.27, 3.30, Corollaries 3.25, 3.26, 3.31 and the construction before Lemma 3.30.

## Conventions

- $\mathbb N=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$. A *truncation set* is a subset $S\subseteq\mathbb N$ such that $n\in S$ and $d\mid n$
  imply $d\in S$. We write $S/n=\{d: nd\in S\}$ and $\langle m\rangle$ for the set of divisors of $m$.
  Following Wagner, $W_m:=W_{\langle m\rangle}$. Thus $W_{p^n}$ is the ring of $p$-typical Witt vectors of
  length $n+1$ (Wagner Remark 2.7), which is Mathlib's `TruncatedWittVector p (n+1)`.
- Ghost components are $w_n(a)=\sum_{d\mid n} d\,a_d^{n/d}$. The power-series isomorphism is
  $\gamma(a)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-a_nt^n)^{-1}$ (Hesselholt Proposition 1.14).
- Rings are commutative. Big Witt vectors and $q$-Witt vectors are defined on commutative rings that need not
  be unital (Wagner §2.2), because the kernels of surjections are used (Wagner Corollary 2.29). "Ring" alone
  means a unital ring.
- A *Λ-ring* is a ring $A$ with a ring map $\lambda_A:A\to W(A)$ that makes $A$ a coalgebra for the
  comonad $(W,\Delta,w_1)$ (Hesselholt Definition 1.21), i.e. an arithmetic (special) λ-ring. It is not
  an Iwasawa algebra. Its Adams operations are $\psi^n=w_n\circ\lambda_A$ (Hesselholt Definition 1.23).
  Mathlib's `BinomialRing` is not used as a definition of λ-rings.
- $[n]_q=1+q+\dots+q^{n-1}$ and $\Phi_d(q)$ is `Polynomial.cyclotomic d ℤ`. We write
  $R[\zeta_d]:=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z[q]/\Phi_d(q)$, where $\zeta_d$ is the class of $q$; no embedding
  into a field is chosen. The Frobenius twist along $\psi^d$ is written $R\otimes_{A,\psi^d}A$, and $A[q]$
  carries the Λ-structure with $\psi^d(q)=q^d$.
- $q\text{-}W_m(R)$ has Frobenii $F_{m/d}$, Verschiebungen $V_{m/d}$, ghost maps $\mathrm{gh}_{m/d}$ and
  Teichmüller lifts $\tau_m$ ($d\mid m$). There are no restriction maps on $q$-Witt vectors.
- A Λ-ring $A$ is *perfectly covered* if $A\to A_\infty:=\operatorname{colim}_{(\mathbb N,\mid)}A$, the colimit along the Adams
  operations, is faithfully flat (Wagner Remark 2.47).
- Derived completions, staticity ("concentrated in degree $0$"), $E_\infty$-algebras and animation are
  those of `DerivedDeRhamCohomology` DD.0–DD.1 and `EnhancedDerivedSheaves` E5.

## Sources

Wagner, *q-Witt vectors and q-Hodge complexes* (arXiv:2410.23078v5), all sections. Wagner, *q-Hodge
complexes over the Habiro ring* (arXiv:2510.04782v2), 1.22(e), §3.4 and the construction before Lemma 3.30.
Hesselholt, *The big de Rham–Witt complex*, §1. Borger, *The basic geometry of Witt vectors I*, §1.
Bhatt–Scholze, *Prisms and prismatic cohomology*, §2 (as imported through PR.0). W. J. G. Ong's notes of
P. Scholze's course *V5A4 – Habiro cohomology* (Bonn, summer 2025), Lectures 2–5, for the framed
definitions and the uncompleted statements.

## Layers

- **QW.0** Big Witt vectors on truncation sets.
- **QW.1** Λ-rings, Adams operations and perfectly covered Λ-rings.
- **QW.2** Absolute $q$-Witt vectors: $q$-FV-systems, ghost maps, Koszul exactness and injectivity.
- **QW.3** $q$-Witt vectors of Λ-rings and relative $q$-Witt vectors.
- **QW.4** $q$-Witt vectors and étale morphisms.
- **QW.5** $q$-de Rham–Witt complexes: universal properties, Frobenii, étale base change.
- **QW.6** Framed $q$-de Rham and $q$-Hodge complexes and the smooth comparison theorem.
- **QW.7** Animated $q$-de Rham–Witt complexes, Nygaard filtrations and the no-go theorem.

## Boundaries

- `PrismaticCohomology` PR.0 owns δ-rings, Frobenius lifts, Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.28 (torsion in δ-rings) and
  Lemma 2.18 (unique extension of δ-structures along $p$-completely étale maps).
- `HabiroCyclotomicCompletions` HC.4 owns the cyclotomic comaximality lemma: $\mathbb Z[q]/(\Phi_m,\Phi_n)=0$
  unless $m=n$ or $m/n$ is a prime power $p^{\pm\alpha}$ with $\alpha\ge1$, and in the latter case it is
  $\mathbb F_p[q]/\Phi_{\min(m,n)}$ (Wagner Lemma 2.1, whose last clause is stated for all $\alpha\in\mathbb Z$ but holds for
  $\alpha\ne0$).
- `CrystallineCohomology` CR.4 owns the Langer–Zink relative de Rham–Witt complex; CR.2–CR.3 own the
  crystalline comparison and Frobenius.
- `HabiroRings` HR.2–HR.5 own Habiro completion, the glued rings $\mathcal H_{R/A,m}$ and $\mathcal H_{R/A}$ and
  their Taylor presentation. This roadmap supplies $q\text{-}W_m(R/A)$ with its Frobenii and étale base change
  to HR.4.
- `HabiroCohomologyFoundations` HQ.1–HQ.4 own the following: the $q$-de Rham complex as a coordinate-independent
  functor (Wagner, arXiv:2510.04782v2, Appendix A); derived $q$-de Rham complexes; $q$-Hodge filtrations and
  Habiro–Hodge complexes; the twisted $q$-de Rham complexes $q\Omega^{(m)}$ with their Nygaard filtrations
  (arXiv:2510.04782v2, 3.14–3.20, Proposition 3.22, Lemma 3.29); $q$-connections; the framed Habiro ring
  $\mathcal H_{(R,\square)}$ with its $q$-Habiro–Hodge complex; and the V5A4 variant of the no-go theorem
  (Theorem 5.7). HQ consumes QW.6 and QW.7.
- `PrismaticCohomology` PR.6 owns the $q$-crystalline site and the $p$-complete comparison of framed
  $q$-de Rham complexes with prismatic cohomology. Its $p$-complete framed complexes over $\mathbb Z_p[[q-1]]$ are the
  completed base changes of QW.6's framed complexes for $A=\mathbb Z$; PR.6 builds them without importing QW, and
  `HabiroCohomologyFoundations` HQ.1 records the comparison.

## Non-goals

The big de Rham–Witt complex of Hesselholt–Madsen (Hesselholt §§2–4) is not built here. Neither are
Chatzistamatiou's unpublished $q$-Witt vectors of Λ-rings (Wagner Remark 1.2) or an untruncated $q$-Witt ring,
which does not exist (Wagner 2.14). The relation of $q$-Witt vectors and $q$-Hodge complexes with
$\mathrm{THH}(-/\mathrm{ku})$ and refined $\mathrm{TC}^-$ belongs to `RefinedTraceMethods`.

stages.title: Big Witt vectors on truncation sets
stages.description:
Big Witt vectors on truncation sets (Hesselholt, *The big de Rham–Witt complex*, §1; Borger, *The basic
geometry of Witt vectors I*).

**Targets.**
- *Witt vectors.* For a truncation set $S$, the functor $W_S$ on commutative, not necessarily unital rings has
  underlying set $A^S$. Its ring structure is the unique natural one that makes the ghost map
  $w:W_S(A)\to A^S$ a ring homomorphism (Hesselholt Proposition 1.2); the Witt polynomials have no constant terms.
  Also: the Dwork lemma characterising the image of $w$ for rings with Frobenius lifts $\varphi_p$ (Lemma 1.1);
  injectivity of $w$ for $\mathbb Z$-torsion-free $A$; restriction maps $R^S_T$ for $T\subseteq S$;
  $W_S=\lim_T W_T$ over finite $T\subseteq S$.
- *Operators.* The additive Verschiebung $V_n:W_{S/n}(A)\to W_S(A)$ (Lemma 1.3). The Frobenius
  $F_n:W_S(A)\to W_{S/n}(A)$, the unique natural ring map lifting reindexing of ghost components (Lemma 1.4).
  The Teichmüller map $a\mapsto[a]_S$. The identities of Lemma 1.5: $a=\sum_{n\in S}V_n([a_n]_{S/n})$;
  $F_mV_n=c\,V_{n/c}F_{m/c}$ with $c=\gcd(m,n)$; $a\,V_n(a')=V_n(F_n(a)a')$; $F_mF_n=F_{mn}$;
  $V_mV_n=V_{mn}$; $F_n[a]=[a^n]$. For finite $S$ and maximal $n\in S$, with $T=S\setminus\{n\}$, the exact
  sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{V_n}W_S(A)\to W_T(A)\to0$.
- *Structure.* $W_S(\mathbb Z)=\prod_{n\in S}\mathbb Z\cdot V_n([1]_{S/n})$ with
  $V_m[1]\cdot V_n[1]=\gcd(m,n)\,V_{\mathrm{lcm}(m,n)}[1]$ (Proposition 1.6). An integer that is invertible
  (resp. a non-zero-divisor) in $A$ remains so in $W_S(A)$ (Lemma 1.9). For $\mathbb F_p$-algebras,
  $F_p=R^S_{S/p}\circ W_S(\varphi)$ (Lemma 1.8) and $V_pF_p=p$ (Lemma 1.12). The $p$-typical decomposition
  $W_S(A)\cong\prod_{k\in I(S)}W_{(S/k)\cap P}(A)$ when every $k\in I(S)$ is invertible in $A$
  (Proposition 1.10). The comparison of $W_{\{1,p,\dots,p^n\}}$ and $W_{\{1,p,p^2,\dots\}}$ with Mathlib's
  `TruncatedWittVector p (n+1)` and `WittVector p`, matching ghost maps, $F_p$, $V_p$ and Teichmüller maps
  (Wagner Remark 2.7).
- *Power series and comonad.* The natural group isomorphism
  $\gamma:W(A)\to(1+tA[[t]])^\times$, $\gamma(a)=\prod_n(1-a_nt^n)^{-1}$, with
  $t\,\tfrac{d}{dt}\log\gamma(a)=\sum_n w_n(a)t^n$ (Proposition 1.14). The natural ring map
  $\Delta:W(A)\to W(W(A))$ with $w_n\circ\Delta=F_n$, together with the comonad identities (Proposition 1.19).
- *Étale base change.* For an étale map $f:A\to B$, a finite truncation set $S$ and $n\ge1$, $W_S(f)$ is étale
  and $W_S(B)\otimes_{W_S(A),F_n}W_{S/n}(A)\to W_{S/n}(B)$ is an isomorphism (Hesselholt Theorem 1.25).

**Inputs.** Mathlib's $p$-typical Witt vectors: `WittVector`, `WittVector.ghostMap`, `WittVector.frobenius`,
`WittVector.verschiebung`, `WittVector.teichmuller`, `TruncatedWittVector`. Also `MvPolynomial`,
`PowerSeries`, `Algebra.Etale` and `Algebra.FormallyEtale`. No atlas stage is needed.

**Acceptance.** $W_{\{1\}}(A)=A$. The ghost map is an isomorphism $W_{\langle m\rangle}(\mathbb Q)\cong\mathbb Q^{\langle m\rangle}$.
The ghost map identifies $W_{\{1,p\}}(\mathbb Z)$ with $\{(x,y)\in\mathbb Z^2:y\equiv x^p\bmod p\}$.
$W_{\{1,\dots,p^n\}}(\mathbb F_p)\cong\mathbb Z/p^{n+1}$, as Mathlib computes for truncated Witt vectors. The
Teichmüller map is multiplicative and not additive.

stages.title: Λ-rings, Adams operations and perfectly covered Λ-rings
stages.description:
Λ-rings, Adams operations and perfectly covered Λ-rings (Hesselholt 1.19–1.24; Borger §1; Wagner 2.31–2.32,
2.38 and Remark 2.47; Wagner, *q-Hodge complexes over the Habiro ring*, 1.22(e)).

**Targets.**
- *Λ-rings.* Λ-rings and their morphisms (Hesselholt Definition 1.21). $W(A)$ is the cofree Λ-ring on $A$,
  i.e. $W$ is right adjoint to the forgetful functor. Free Λ-rings on a set are polynomial rings over
  $\mathbb Z$, hence $\mathbb Z$-flat, and every Λ-ring is a quotient of a free one by a Λ-ideal. Λ-ideals,
  quotients, tensor products, and localisations at multiplicative sets stable under all $\psi^p$.
- *Adams operations.* $\psi^n=w_n\circ\lambda$ is a ring endomorphism with $\psi^1=\mathrm{id}$,
  $\psi^m\psi^n=\psi^{mn}$ and $\psi^p(a)\equiv a^p\bmod pA$ (Lemma 1.24). On the cofree Λ-ring,
  $\psi^n=F_n$.
- *Wilkerson's criterion.* For $\mathbb Z$-torsion-free $A$, Λ-structures correspond bijectively to families
  $(\psi^p)_p$ of pairwise commuting ring endomorphisms with $\psi^p(a)\equiv a^p\bmod p$. A Λ-structure
  induces for every prime $p$ a δ-structure on $A$ and on $A_{(p)}$ with Frobenius $\psi^p$, compatible with
  PR.0.
- *Truncated structures.* Λ$_m$-rings, which carry Adams operations only for divisors of $m$ (Wagner
  Remark 2.32), and the trivial Λ$_m$-structure on a ring in which $m$ is invertible (Wagner Example 2.38).
- *Trivial sections.* The section $s=\lambda:A\to W(A)$ of $w_1$, its truncations $s_m:A\to W_m(A)$, and
  $\psi^m=w_m\circ s$ (Wagner 2.31).
- *Examples.* $\mathbb Z$ and $\mathbb Z_p$ with $\psi^n=\mathrm{id}$. Monoid algebras $\mathbb Z[M]$ with
  $\psi^n(x)=x^n$ for $x\in M$, in particular $\mathbb Z[T_1,\dots,T_d]$, $\mathbb Z[T_1^{\pm1},\dots,T_d^{\pm1}]$ and
  $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1}]$. The Λ-structure on $A[q]$ and $A[q^{\pm1}]$ extending that of $A$ by
  $\psi^n(q)=q^n$. $\mathbb Z[\zeta_N,1/N]$ with $\psi^p(\zeta_N)=\zeta_N^p$ for $p\nmid N$ and $\psi^p=\mathrm{id}$
  for $p\mid N$.
- *Perfect and perfectly covered Λ-rings.* $A$ is perfect if every $\psi^p$ is bijective. The colimit
  perfection $A_\infty$ is the universal perfect Λ-ring under $A$. $A$ is perfectly covered if
  $A\to A_\infty$ is faithfully flat (Wagner Remark 2.47). Equivalently, there is a faithfully flat Λ-map from $A$ to some
  perfect Λ-ring, and equivalently every $\psi^m$ is faithfully flat (the footnote to Remark 2.47; *q-Hodge complexes over
  the Habiro ring*, 1.22(e)). A perfect Λ-ring is $\mathbb Z$-torsion-free: apply
  Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.28 to $A_{(p)}$, as in Wagner's proof of Proposition 2.36. A perfectly covered Λ-ring
  is $\mathbb Z$-torsion-free and $A/p$ is reduced for every $p$ (Wagner 4.9). $\mathbb Z$,
  $\mathbb Z[T_1,\dots,T_d]$ and $\mathbb Z[T_1^{\pm1},\dots,T_d^{\pm1}]$ (so also $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1}]$) are
  perfectly covered, with $A_\infty$ the monoid algebra of $\mathbb Q_{\ge0}^d$, resp. $\mathbb Q^d$, which is
  free over $A$. Every free Λ-ring $\mathbb Z\{x_i\mid i\in I\}$ is perfectly covered (*q-Hodge complexes over the Habiro ring*,
  1.22(e)).

**Inputs.** QW.0. From `PrismaticCohomology` PR.0: δ-rings, Frobenius lifts and Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.28.

**Acceptance.** Every Λ-ring $A$ with $pA=0$ is zero, because $p=V_pF_p(1)=V_p(1)\neq0$ in $W(A)$ for
$A\neq0$. The ideal $(\Phi_m(q))\subseteq\mathbb Z[q]$ is not $\psi^p$-stable for $p\mid m$, so
$q\mapsto\zeta_m$ does not make $\mathbb Z[\zeta_m]$ a Λ-quotient of $\mathbb Z[q]$. $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1/\infty}]$
is the perfection of $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1}]$. $\mathbb Z[\zeta_N,1/N]$ is a perfect Λ-ring.

stages.title: Absolute q-Witt vectors
stages.description:
Absolute $q$-Witt vectors (Wagner, *q-Witt vectors and q-Hodge complexes*, §§2.1–2.3).

**Targets.**
- *Preliminaries* (§2.1). Lemma 2.2: for every $m$, $\big([p]_{q^{m/p}}: p\text{ a prime factor of }m\big)=(\Phi_m(q))$
  in $\mathbb Z[q]$. Lemma 2.3: finite families of elements generating unit ideals. Lemma 2.4: if
  finitely generated ideals $I_j$ and elements $f_k$ satisfy
  $\operatorname{Spec}R=\bigcup_jV(I_j)\cup\bigcup_kD(f_k)$, then the functors $(-)^\wedge_{I_j}$ and
  $(-)[1/f_k]$ on $D(R)$ are jointly conservative. Remark 2.5: $-\otimes^L\mathbb Q$ and all $(-)^\wedge_p$ are
  jointly conservative. Lemma 2.1 (cyclotomic comaximality) is imported from HC.4.
- *Definition* (§2.2). $q$-FV-systems of rings over a commutative, not necessarily unital ring $R$
  (Definition 2.8). Lemma 2.9: the initial object is $q\text{-}W_m(R)=W_m(R)[q]/I_m$, where $I_m$ is generated by
  $(q^d-1)\operatorname{im}V_{m/d}$ and by $\operatorname{im}([d/e]_{q^e}V_{m/d}-V_{m/e}F_{d/e})$ for all
  $e\mid d\mid m$. Definition 2.10 and Remark 2.12, the variant for truncation sets. Remarks 1.2 and 2.11:
  $q\text{-}W_m(R)/(q-1)$ is the universal quotient of $W_m(R)$ in which $V_{m/d}F_{m/d}=m/d$, so
  $q\text{-}W_m(R)$ is not a $q$-deformation of $W_m(R)$.
- *Ghost maps and Teichmüller lifts* (2.13). The isomorphism
  $q\text{-}W_m(R)/(\operatorname{im}V_p: p\mid m)\cong R[q]/\Phi_m(q)$ defines $\mathrm{gh}_{m/m}$. Then
  $\mathrm{gh}_{m/d}:=\mathrm{gh}_{d/d}\circ F_{m/d}:q\text{-}W_m(R)\to R[\zeta_d]$. Teichmüller lifts
  $\tau_m:R\to q\text{-}W_m(R)$.
- *No restrictions* (2.14). Let $R=\mathbb Z$, $m=p^\alpha$ with $\alpha\ge1$, and $d=p^{\alpha-1}$. There is no
  $\mathbb Z[q]$-algebra map $q\text{-}W_m(R)\to q\text{-}W_d(R)$ compatible with Verschiebungen, because
  $\Phi_{p^\alpha}(\zeta_{p^{\alpha-1}})=p\neq0$. Hence there is no untruncated $q$-Witt ring.
- *Koszul exactness.* Proposition 2.15 with Remark 2.16, Lemma 2.17 (the prime-power case) and Lemma 2.18 (the
  hypercube lemma): the augmented Koszul complex
  $\cdots\to\bigoplus_{i<j}q\text{-}W_{m/p_ip_j}(R)\to\bigoplus_iq\text{-}W_{m/p_i}(R)\to q\text{-}W_m(R)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{gh}_{m/m}}R[\zeta_m]\to0$
  is exact.
- *Consequences.* Corollary 2.19: every $V_{m/d}$ is injective. Corollary 2.20: localisation at $U\subseteq\mathbb Z$,
  and at $U\subseteq R$ through $\tau_m$. Lemma 2.21: over a $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$-algebra, an element killed by $\mathrm{gh}_{m/m}$
  and by every $F_\ell$ with $\ell\ne p$ lies in the image of $V_p$. Corollary 2.22: $p$-torsion-freeness
  passes from $R$ to $q\text{-}W_m(R)$. Lemma 2.23: the ghost maps $\mathrm{gh}_{m/d}$ are jointly injective when $R$
  is $p$-torsion-free for all $p\mid m$. Corollary 2.24: $q\text{-}W_m(R)^\wedge_p\simeq q\text{-}W_m(\widehat R_p)$ when
  $\widehat R_p$ is static, and derived $p$-completeness is inherited. Corollary 2.26 with Lemma 2.27: the derived
  $(q^n-1)$-completion is static, and $(q^n-1)^\infty$-torsion is bounded if $R$ has bounded $p^\infty$-torsion for
  $p\mid m$. Lemma 2.30: for $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$-algebras and $m=p^\alpha n$ with $p\nmid n$,
  $q\text{-}W_m(R)\cong\prod_{d\mid n}q\text{-}W_{p^\alpha}(R)\otimes_{\mathbb Z_{(p)}[q],\psi^d}\mathbb Z_{(p)}[q]/\Phi_d(q^{p^\alpha})$.
- *Injectivity of $W_m\to q\text{-}W_m$* (§2.3). Proposition 2.28. Corollary 2.29: for a surjection $R\to R'$ with
  kernel $J$, the sequence $0\to q\text{-}W_m(J)\to q\text{-}W_m(R)\to q\text{-}W_m(R')\to0$ is exact.
- *Ghost square* (V5A4 Proposition 4.15 and Remark 4.16). For flat $R$, the ghost components
  $W_m(R)\to\prod_{d\mid m}R$ and the $q$-ghost maps $q\text{-}W_m(R)\to\prod_{d\mid m}R[\zeta_d]$ form a commutative
  square, with the $d$-th factor sent to the $(m/d)$-th.

**Inputs.** QW.0. From `HabiroCyclotomicCompletions` HC.4: the comaximality lemma (Wagner Lemma 2.1). From
`DerivedDeRhamCohomology` DD.1: derived completion, derived Nakayama and conservativity of reductions. From
`EnhancedDerivedSheaves` E5:abstract: the stable ∞-categorical cofibre arguments in the proof of Corollary 2.19.

**Acceptance.** $q\text{-}W_1(R)=R$. $q\text{-}W_p(\mathbb Z)$ is the quotient of $W_p(\mathbb Z)[q]$ by
$(q-1)\operatorname{im}V_p$, $(q^p-1)$ and the image of $[p]_q-V_pF_p$ (Lemma 2.9 for $m=p$), it is isomorphic to
$\mathbb Z[q]/(q^p-1)$ (Corollary 2.37), and $(\mathrm{gh}_{p/p},\mathrm{gh}_{p/1})$ embeds it in $\mathbb Z[\zeta_p]\times\mathbb Z$.
There is no restriction map for $R=\mathbb Z$ and $m=p$. $W_4(\mathbb Z)\to q\text{-}W_4(\mathbb Z)$ is injective.
The Koszul complex for $m=6$ is written out.

stages.title: q-Witt vectors of Λ-rings and relative q-Witt vectors
stages.description:
$q$-Witt vectors of Λ-rings and relative $q$-Witt vectors (Wagner §§2.4–2.5).

**Targets.**
- *Comparison maps for Λ-rings* (§2.4). The trivial map $s_m:A[q]/(q^m-1)\to q\text{-}W_m(A)$ (2.31) and
  Remark 2.32. Lemma 2.33: the natural maps $\varepsilon_m:W_m(A)\to A$ with
  $w_m(x)=\sum_{d\mid m}d\,\psi^{m/d}\big(\varepsilon_d(\mathrm{Res}_{m/d}x)\big)$. Lemma 2.34: the map
  $c_m(x)=\sum_{d\mid m}[d]_{q^{m/d}}\psi^{m/d}\big(\varepsilon_d(\mathrm{Res}_{m/d}x)\big)$ is a ring map
  $W_m(A)\to A[q]/(q^m-1)$. Corollary 2.35: $c_m$ extends uniquely to $q\text{-}W_m(A)$, carrying $F_{m/d}$ to the
  projection and $V_{m/d}$ to multiplication by $[m/d]_{q^d}$, and $c_m\circ s_m=\psi^m$.
  Proposition 2.36: if every $\psi^m$ is injective, $c_m$ is an isomorphism onto
  $\sum_{d\mid m}[d]_{q^{m/d}}\psi^{m/d}(A)[q]/(q^m-1)$. Corollary 2.37: for perfect $A$, $s_m$ and $c_m$ are
  isomorphisms; in particular $q\text{-}W_m(\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z[q]/(q^m-1)$. Example 2.38, the Λ$_m$-variant. Corollary 2.39:
  if $R$ is of finite type over $\mathbb Z$, then $q\text{-}W_m(R)$ is of finite type over $\mathbb Z[q]/(q^m-1)$,
  hence noetherian.
- *Relative $q$-Witt vectors* (§2.5). For a Λ-ring $A$ and an $A$-algebra $R$: $q$-FV-systems of $A$-algebras
  over $R$ (Definition 2.40). Lemma 2.41: the initial object is
  $q\text{-}W_m(R/A)=\big(q\text{-}W_m(R)\otimes_{q\text{-}W_m(A),c_m}A[q]/(q^m-1)\big)/U_m$. Definition 2.42.
  Remark 2.43 (truncation sets).
- *Relative ghost and comparison maps* (2.44–2.45). Relative ghost maps
  $\mathrm{gh}_{m/d}:q\text{-}W_m(R/A)\to R\otimes_{A,\psi^d}A[q]/\Phi_d(q)$ with
  $\mathrm{gh}_{m/d}=\mathrm{gh}_{d/d}\circ F_{m/d}$; $\mathrm{gh}_{m/m}$ is the quotient by the images of all proper
  Verschiebungen. For Λ-$A$-algebras, the map $c_{m/A}:q\text{-}W_m(R/A)\to R[q]/(q^m-1)$. Also
  $s_{m/A}:R\otimes_{A,\psi^m}A[q]/(q^m-1)\to q\text{-}W_m(R/A)$.
- *Base change and perfectly covered bases.* Lemma 2.46: for a map of Λ-rings $A\to A'$,
  $q\text{-}W_m(R/A)\otimes_AA'\cong q\text{-}W_m(R\otimes_AA'/A')$. Remark 2.47: if $A_\infty$ is perfect, then
  $q\text{-}W_m(R)\cong q\text{-}W_m(R/A_\infty)$ for $A_\infty$-algebras $R$. For perfectly covered $A$, faithfully flat
  descent along $A\to A_\infty$ gives relative versions of Proposition 2.15 and Corollaries 2.19, 2.22, 2.24 and 2.26.
  It also shows that $s_{m/A}$ and $c_{m/A}$ are isomorphisms for relatively perfect $R$, i.e. when every
  $R\otimes_{A,\psi^p}A\to R$ is an isomorphism.

**Inputs.** QW.1, QW.2.

**Acceptance.** For $A=\mathbb Z$, $q\text{-}W_m(R/\mathbb Z)=q\text{-}W_m(R)$. $q\text{-}W_m(\mathbb Z[T])$ is the subring
$\sum_{d\mid m}[d]_{q^{m/d}}\mathbb Z[T^{m/d},q]/(q^m-1)$ of $\mathbb Z[T,q]/(q^m-1)$ (proof of Corollary 2.39). For
$A=\mathbb Z[T^{\pm1}]$, $q\text{-}W_m(A/A)\cong A[q]/(q^m-1)$. Both sides of Lemma 2.46 are computed for
$A=\mathbb Z\to A'=\mathbb Z[T]$ and $R=\mathbb Z[x]$.

stages.title: q-Witt vectors and étale morphisms
stages.description:
$q$-Witt vectors and étale morphisms (Wagner §2.6).

**Targets.**
- *Étale base change* (Proposition 2.48). For a Λ-ring $A$, an étale map $R\to R'$ of $A$-algebras and $m\ge1$,
  $q\text{-}W_m(R/A)\to q\text{-}W_m(R'/A)$ is étale. For every $d\mid m$, with the tensor product taken along
  $F_{m/d}$,
  $q\text{-}W_m(R'/A)\otimes_{q\text{-}W_m(R/A),F_{m/d}}q\text{-}W_d(R/A)\cong q\text{-}W_d(R'/A)$.
  Remark 2.49 records the ordinary Witt vector analogue from QW.0.
- *Comparison with Witt vectors* (Lemma 2.50).
  $W_m(R')\otimes_{W_m(R)}q\text{-}W_m(R/A)\cong q\text{-}W_m(R'/A)$.
- *Ghost pushouts* (Corollary 2.51). For every $d\mid m$, the square formed by $q\text{-}W_m(R/A)\to q\text{-}W_m(R'/A)$
  and the ghost maps to $R\otimes_{A,\psi^d}A[\zeta_d]\to R'\otimes_{A,\psi^d}A[\zeta_d]$ is a pushout, both
  derived and underived.
- *The Frobenius obstruction* (Corollary 2.52). Let $R$ be an étale $\mathbb Z$-algebra with $R\to\widehat R_p$ injective.
  Suppose a $\mathbb Z[q]$-algebra isomorphism $q\text{-}W_m(R)\cong R[q]/(q^m-1)$ exists for some $m$ divisible by $p$.
  Then the unique Frobenius lift $\varphi_p$ of $\widehat R_p$ restricts to an endomorphism of $R$. These
  endomorphisms commute for different $p$, and $R$ carries a Λ$_m$-structure.

**Inputs.** QW.3. QW.0 supplies étale base change for $W_S$. Through QW.1, `PrismaticCohomology` PR.0 supplies
the unique Frobenius lift on $\widehat R_p$ (Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.18).

**Acceptance.** For $R=\mathbb Z[\zeta_N,1/N]$, a perfect Λ-ring, $q\text{-}W_m(R)\cong R[q]/(q^m-1)$ (Corollary 2.37).
For $R=\mathbb Z[\sqrt[3]2,1/6]$ and $m=5$ no such isomorphism exists: $\mathbb Q(\sqrt[3]2)$ has no
nontrivial automorphism and $5$ does not split completely in it, so Corollary 2.52 applies. The étale map
$\mathbb Z[T]\to\mathbb Z[T,T^{-1}]$ is checked against Proposition 2.48 for $m=p$.

stages.title: q-de Rham–Witt complexes
stages.description:
$q$-de Rham–Witt complexes (Wagner §3).

**Targets.**
- *Three categories* (§3.1). $q$-V-systems of differential-graded $A$-algebras over an $A$-algebra $R$, with the
  $V$-Teichmüller condition $(\tau_V)$ (Definition 3.1). Lemma 3.2: $V_n\circ d=n\,(d\circ V_n)$. The
  $V$-divided powers of 3.3. Lemma 3.4: $q\text{-}W_m(R)\to P^1_m$ is a $V$-PD-derivation and
  $dV_p(x^p)=V_p(x^{p-1})\,dV_p(x)$. Remark 3.5. $q$-FV-systems (Definition 3.6), whose Frobenii satisfy
  $F_{m/d}\circ d\circ V_{m/d}=d$ and $V_{m/d}(\omega F_{m/d}(\eta))=V_{m/d}(\omega)\eta$; Lemma 3.7 and Remark 3.8.
  Torsion-free $q$-V-systems (Definition 3.9), with the fully faithful inclusion of Remark 3.10.
- *No restriction maps* (3.11). Neither the $q$-theory nor the Langer–Zink de Rham–Witt pro-complex needs
  restriction maps: the latter is initial among $F$-$V$-systems without restrictions.
- *Construction* (§3.2). Proposition 3.12: the initial $q$-V-system $(q\text{-}W_m\Omega^*_{R/A})_m$ exists;
  $\Omega^*_{q\text{-}W_m(R/A)/A[q]}\to q\text{-}W_m\Omega^*_{R/A}$ is surjective;
  $q\text{-}W_1\Omega^*_{R/A}=\Omega^*_{R/A}$; the degree-zero part is $q\text{-}W_m(R/A)$. Definition 3.13 and
  Remark 3.14. The ghost maps of dg algebras
  $\mathrm{gh}_{m/d}:q\text{-}W_m\Omega^*_{R/A}\to\Omega^*_{R/A}\otimes_{A,\psi^d}A[\zeta_d]$ (3.15). Lemma 3.16: base
  change along maps of Λ-rings.
- *Frobenii* (§3.3). Proposition 3.17: there are unique Frobenii making the system a $q$-FV-system, and it is
  initial among $q$-FV-systems. The proof (3.19–3.30) comprises Lemma 3.21, the map $F_pd$ of
  Construction 3.22, Lemmas 3.23–3.26, Construction 3.27 and Lemmas 3.28–3.30.
- *Langer–Zink comparison* (Remark 3.18). For a $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$-algebra $A$, maps
  $W_{\alpha+1}\Omega^*_{R/A}\to q\text{-}W_{p^\alpha}\Omega^*_{R/A}$ compatible with $F$ and $V$. They come from the
  restriction-free universal property of 3.11 applied to CR.4's relative de Rham–Witt complex.
- *Étale base change* (§3.4). Proposition 3.31:
  $q\text{-}W_m(R'/A)\otimes_{q\text{-}W_m(R/A)}q\text{-}W_m\Omega^*_{R/A}\cong q\text{-}W_m\Omega^*_{R'/A}$ for étale $R\to R'$.
  Lemma 3.32: dg structures on étale base changes. Corollary 3.33: each
  $q\text{-}W_m\Omega_{-/A}:\mathrm{CRing}_A\to\mathrm{CAlg}(D(A[q]))$ is an étale sheaf. Corollary 3.34, the rational
  ghost isomorphism
  $q\text{-}W_m\Omega^*_{R/A}[1/m]\cong\prod_{d\mid m}\Omega^*_{R/A}\otimes_{A,\psi^d}A[1/m,\zeta_d]$.
- *Distinction* (V5A4 Remark 5.5). $q\text{-}W_m\Omega^*_R$ differs from the de Rham complex $\Omega^*_{q\text{-}W_m(R)}$ of
  the $q$-Witt vectors.

**Inputs.** QW.4. From `CrystallineCohomology` CR.4: the Langer–Zink relative de Rham–Witt complex and its
universal property. From `EnhancedDerivedSheaves`: E1 and E2 for derived étale descent of bounded below
complexes (Corollary 3.33), and E5:abstract for $E_\infty$-algebras.

**Acceptance.** For $m=1$ the complex is $\Omega^*_{R/A}$. For $R=A$ with $A$ perfectly covered, it is
$A[q]/(q^m-1)$ in degree $0$ and zero in positive degrees. For $R=\mathbb Z[T]$, $A=\mathbb Z$ and $m=p$, compute the
image of the ghost maps in $\Omega^*_{\mathbb Z[T]}\times\Omega^*_{\mathbb Z[T]}\otimes_{\psi^p}\mathbb Z[\zeta_p]$. The
Langer–Zink comparison for $m=p$ and $A=\mathbb Z_{(p)}$.

stages.title: Framed q-de Rham and q-Hodge complexes and the smooth comparison theorem
stages.description:
Framed $q$-de Rham and $q$-Hodge complexes and the smooth comparison theorem (Wagner §4; the framed definitions
of V5A4 Lectures 2–3).

**Targets.**
- *Framings and $q$-derivatives.* Let $A$ be a Λ-ring and $R$ a smooth $A$-algebra with an étale framing
  $\square:A[T_1,\dots,T_n]\to R$, or a toric framing $A[T_1^{\pm1},\dots,T_n^{\pm1}]\to R$ (V5A4 Definition 2.1).
  Infinitesimal lifting gives the automorphisms $\gamma_i$ of $R[[q-1]]$ that lift $T_j\mapsto q^{\delta_{ij}}T_j$
  (Wagner 4.7; V5A4 Remarks 2.4–2.5). They are congruent to the identity modulo $(q-1)T_i$ and pairwise commute.
  From them: the $q$-derivatives $q\text{-}\partial_if=(\gamma_if-f)/(qT_i-T_i)$ (V5A4 Definition 2.3); the
  logarithmic $q$-derivatives $(\gamma_i-1)/(q-1)$ for toric framings (V5A4 Definitions 3.1–3.2, Example 3.4);
  and the twisted Leibniz rule $q\text{-}\partial_i(fg)=f\,q\text{-}\partial_ig+\gamma_i(g)\,q\text{-}\partial_if$
  (V5A4 Lemma 2.6; Wagner 4.8).
- *Framed complexes.* The framed $q$-de Rham complex $q\Omega^*_{R/A,\square}$ is the Koszul complex of the
  $q\text{-}\partial_i$ (V5A4 Definition 2.7). The framed $q$-Hodge complex $q\mathrm{Hdg}^*_{R/A,\square}$ is the Koszul
  complex of the $(q-1)\,q\text{-}\partial_i$, i.e. of the modified $q$-derivatives (V5A4 Definitions 2.10 and 2.12).
  Both carry the non-commutative dg algebra structures of Wagner 4.8. Moreover
  $q\Omega^*_{R/A,\square}/(q-1)\cong\Omega^*_{R/A}$ and $q\Omega^*_{R/A,\square}\cong\eta_{(q-1)}q\mathrm{Hdg}^*_{R/A,\square}$
  (Wagner 1.6, Berthelot–Ogus décalage). The framed Frobenius lift $\varphi_\square$ on $\widehat R_p$ is injective
  (Wagner 4.9).
- *Smooth $q$-de Rham–Witt complexes* (§4.1). Proposition 4.1: degree-wise $\mathbb Z$-torsion-free, and initial
  among torsion-free $q$-V-systems. Proposition 4.2: for $m=p^\alpha n$ with $p\nmid n$ there are $p$-complete
  $E_\infty$-equivalences, functorial in smooth $R$,
  $\prod_{d\mid n}\big(\Omega_{R/A}\otimes^L_{A,\psi^{p^\alpha d}}A[q]/\Phi_d(q^{p^\alpha})\big)^\wedge_p\simeq(q\text{-}W_m\Omega_{R/A})^\wedge_p$.
  Remark 4.4, Lemma 4.5, and Lemma 4.6 (bounded $(q-1)^\infty$-torsion).
- *The $q$-Hodge complex modulo $q^m-1$* (§§4.2–4.3). The Frobenius decompositions 4.10–4.14 and Corollary 4.15.
  The dg algebra structure 4.16. The arithmetic fracture pullback squares 4.18. Lemmas 4.19 and 4.21,
  Construction 4.22, Lemmas 4.24–4.25. Construction 4.26: a $q$-FV-system structure on
  $H^*_{R/A,\square}(m):=H^*(q\mathrm{Hdg}^*_{R/A,\square}/(q^m-1))$ and the induced morphism
  $(q\text{-}W_m\Omega^*_{R/A})^\wedge_{(q-1)}\to H^*_{R/A,\square}(m)$.
- *Main theorem* (Theorem 4.27). For $R$ smooth over a perfectly covered Λ-ring $A$, the morphism of
  Construction 4.26 is an isomorphism for every $m$. The case $A=\mathbb Z$ is Wagner Theorem 1.7 and the
  $(q-1)$-completed form of V5A4 Theorem 1.3. In degree zero,
  $H^0(q\mathrm{Hdg}^*_{R/A,\square}/(q^m-1))\cong q\text{-}W_m(R/A)^\wedge_{(q-1)}$, independently of the framing.
- *Proof* (§§4.4–4.6). The Frobenius on the $q$-Hodge complex (4.28). Lemmas 4.29, 4.30 and 4.32. The
  non-canonical quasi-isomorphisms 4.31 and 4.33. The functorial comparison 4.34 through a PD-envelope, and
  Remark 4.35. Lemma 4.36:
  $q\text{-}W_m\Omega^*_{R/A,(p)}\cong\prod_{d\mid n}q\text{-}W_{p^\alpha}\Omega^*_{R/A}\otimes_{A[q],\psi^d}A_{(p)}[q]/\Phi_d(q^{p^\alpha})$.
  Corollary 4.37: the arithmetic fracture square of $q\text{-}W_m\Omega_{R/A}$, involving the crystalline relative
  Frobenius $\varphi_{p/A}$. Corollary 4.38: $\widetilde F_p$ is compatible with $\varphi_{p/A}$.

**Inputs.** QW.5. From `AInfCohomology` AI.1: décalage, both $L\eta$ and the underived $\eta$ on torsion-free
complexes. From `DerivedDeRhamCohomology` DD.1: derived completion. From `CrystallineCohomology` CR.3 (through
CR.0 and CR.2): PD-envelopes, $(\Omega_{R/A})^\wedge_p\simeq R\Gamma_{\mathrm{crys}}((R/p)/\widehat A_p)$ and the crystalline
Frobenius.

**Acceptance.** For $R=A[T]$ with the identity framing and $m=p$, both sides are computed explicitly; after
$(q-1)$-completion this recovers V5A4 Example 4.12 and Proposition 4.13. The framings $T$ and $T+1$ of
$\mathbb Z[T]$ give different complexes, whose cohomologies modulo $q^m-1$ Theorem 4.27 identifies compatibly
with $F$ and $V$. The degree-one Bockstein differential recovers $d$.

stages.title: Animated q-de Rham–Witt complexes, Nygaard filtrations and the no-go theorem
stages.description:
Animated $q$-de Rham–Witt complexes, Nygaard filtrations and the no-go theorem (Wagner, *q-Hodge complexes
over the Habiro ring*, 3.21, 3.23–3.28, the construction opening §3.5, and 3.30–3.31; Wagner, *q-Witt vectors and
q-Hodge complexes*, §5).

**Targets.**
- *Animation.* The Hodge$_m$ filtration $\mathrm{fil}^\star_{\mathrm{Hdg}_m}q\text{-}W_m\Omega^*_{S/A}$ is the stupid filtration
  $q\text{-}W_m\Omega^{\ge\star}_{S/A}$. Left Kan extension from polynomial $A$-algebras gives its animation
  $\mathrm{fil}^\star_{\mathrm{Hdg}_m}q\text{-}W_m\mathrm{dR}_{-/A}$, with values in filtered $E_\infty$-$A[q]/(q^m-1)$-algebras on animated
  $A$-algebras, and graded pieces $q\text{-}W_m\mathrm{dR}^n_{-/A}$ (the construction before Lemma 3.30).
- *Nygaard filtration* (3.21). For $m=p^\alpha$, the Nygaard filtration on $q\text{-}W_{p^\alpha}\Omega^*_{S/A}$ is given in
  degree $n$ by $p^{n-1-i}V_p\,q\text{-}W_{p^{\alpha-1}}\Omega^i_{S/A}$ for $i<n$ and all of
  $q\text{-}W_{p^\alpha}\Omega^i_{S/A}$ for $i\ge n$. Lemma 3.23: $\widetilde F_p$ is divisible by $p^n$ on $\mathrm{fil}^n_N$, and
  $p^{-n}\widetilde F_p:\mathrm{gr}^n_N\to\tau^{\le n}(q\text{-}W_{p^{\alpha-1}}\Omega^*_{S/A}/p)$ is surjective in degree $n$ and
  an isomorphism in all other degrees. Lemma 3.24:
  $\Omega^n_{S/A}\otimes_{A,\varphi^\alpha}A[\zeta_{p^\alpha}]\cong\ker F_p$, in both forms stated there.
- *Animated Nygaard filtration.* Corollary 3.25: a divided Frobenius
  $\mathrm{gr}^n_Nq\text{-}W_{p^\alpha}\mathrm{dR}_{R/A}\to\mathrm{fil}^{\mathrm{conj}}_n(\mathrm{dR}_{R/A}/p)\otimes^L_{A,\varphi^{\alpha-1}}A[q]/(q^{p^{\alpha-1}}-1)$
  with fibre $\Sigma^{-n}\mathrm{dR}^n_{R/A}\otimes^L_{A,\varphi^\alpha}A[\zeta_{p^\alpha}]$. Corollary 3.26:
  $p$-completed quasi-syntomic descent, and agreement with the un-animated filtration for smooth $R$. Lemma 3.27
  with Remark 3.28: the second fibre sequence, involving the Hodge filtration of $\mathrm{dR}_{R/A}\otimes A[\zeta_{p^\alpha}]$.
- *Hodge$_m$ and Nygaard filtrations.* Lemma 3.30 relates $\mathrm{fil}^n_{\mathrm{Hdg}_{p^\alpha}}$, $\mathrm{fil}^n_N$ and
  $\mathrm{fil}^n_{\mathrm{Hdg}_{p^{\alpha-1}}}$. Corollary 3.31: for smooth $S$ over $A$, all $m$ and all $n\ge0$,
  $q\text{-}W_m\mathrm{dR}^n_{S/A}\simeq\Sigma^{-n}q\text{-}W_m\Omega^n_{S/A}$.
- *No-go theorem* (Theorem 5.1 with Remarks 5.2–5.3 and 5.4–5.6). Let $A$ be a perfectly covered Λ-ring that is
  not a $\mathbb Q$-algebra. There is no functor $q\mathrm{Hdg}_{-/A}:\mathrm{Sm}_A\to\widehat D_{(q-1)}(A[[q-1]])$ together with
  functorial graded isomorphisms
  $(q\text{-}W_m\Omega^*_{-/A})^\wedge_{(q-1)}\cong H^*(q\mathrm{Hdg}_{-/A}/^L(q^m-1))$ for all $m$ under which the projections
  modulo $q^d-1$ induce $F_{m/d}$. The proof builds: the derived $q$-Hodge complex (5.4); the
  $q$-de Rham–Witt filtration, with graded pieces $(Lq\text{-}W_m\Omega^i)^\wedge_{(q-1)}[-i]$ and zeroth step
  $q\text{-}W_m(R/A)^\wedge_{(q-1)}$ (5.5); Lemma 5.6, the computations for $W=(A_{\inf}(\mathcal O_C)\otimes A)^\wedge_p$
  and $R=W/\xi$; and the contradiction obtained from $\delta(\xi)$ being a unit.

**Inputs.** QW.6. From `DerivedDeRhamCohomology`: DD.0 (cotangent complexes and derived exterior powers, with
$(L\Omega^i_{\mathcal O_C/\mathbb Z_p})^\wedge_p[-i]\simeq\mathcal O_C$ and vanishing of $(L_{A_{\inf}(\mathcal O_C)/\mathbb Z_p})^\wedge_p$), DD.2
(derived de Rham complexes and Hodge filtrations), DD.3 (conjugate filtrations) and DD.5 (quasi-syntomic
descent). From `EnhancedDerivedSheaves` E5:animation: animated rings. From `AInfCohomology` AI.0: $A_{\inf}(\mathcal O_C)$,
$\theta$, a distinguished generator $\xi$ with $\delta(\xi)$ a unit, and the integral perfectoid ring $\mathcal O_C$.

**Acceptance.** For $S=A[T]$ the animated and un-animated Nygaard filtrations agree (Corollary 3.26(b)). For
$m=p$ and $S=\mathbb Z_p[T]$, Lemma 3.24 identifies $\ker F_p$ explicitly. The no-go argument is run for
$A=\mathbb Z$ with $R=\mathcal O_{\mathbb C_p}=A_{\inf}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb C_p})/\xi$: the $m=1$ and $m=p$ steps are checked separately.
